PRs missing backports.title: gh-129724: Intern code object names before merging them with constants
PRs missing backports.body:
The compiler merges the `co_names` and local variable names tuples of a code object with its constant cache, so they can be the same object as an equal tuple constant of an earlier function.  `_PyCode_New()` then interns the items of that shared tuple in place: if an equal string was already interned in the process, the constant's string is replaced by it, otherwise the constant's own string becomes the interned one.  Which constants are the same object, and so the bytes `marshal` writes, depended on what was interned before.  This change interns the names in `makecode()` before the merge.

It needs a name that is not interned yet and is not an ASCII identifier, since the parser interns identifiers and the compiler interns ASCII identifier-like string constants: a private name of a class with a non-ASCII name, which each compilation mangles into a new string, or an identifier of an AST passed to `compile()` that the parser did not create.

```python
import subprocess, sys
src = '''\
class \xc9:
    def g(self):
        return ("_\xc9__x",), "_\xc9__x"
    def f(self):
        return self.__x
'''
child = f'''
import hashlib, marshal, sys
if sys.argv[1] == "interned":
    keep = sys.intern("_\\xc9" + "__x")
print(hashlib.sha256(marshal.dumps(compile({src!r}, "t", "exec"))).hexdigest()[:12])
'''
for state in "fresh", "interned":
    print(state, subprocess.check_output([sys.executable, "-c", child, state], text=True).strip())
```

On main the two digests differ, and compiling the same source twice in one process also gives different bytes.  The free-threaded build was not affected, because it interns all string constants.

Part of gh-129724.

PRs missing backports.title: gh-160708: Use the type size for resized ctypes simple objects
PRs missing backports.body:
After `ctypes.resize()`, the buffer of a simple ctypes object is bigger than the type itself. Two places still used the buffer size (`b_size`) where they needed the type size:

- `Simple_bool_impl()` compared `b_size` bytes against a 16-byte zero string literal. For a resized object it reads past the literal, and it can also return the wrong answer (`bool(c_int(0))` is `True` if the extra space isn't zero).
- `PyCSimpleType_paramfunc()` copied `b_size` bytes into `PyCArgObject.value`, which is a fixed-size union, so passing a resized object to a foreign function overwrote the heap.

Both now use `info->size`, the same as the value getter since gh-159739. `bool()` checks the value's bytes in a loop instead of comparing with the literal. This also covers simple types larger than 16 bytes, such as `c_longdouble_complex` on x86-64.

Tests: `bool()` on a resized `c_int` whose extra space is non-zero, a call to `tf_i` with a resized `c_int`, and `bool()` on the complex types.

PRs missing backports.title: gh-135736: Fix interaction between TaskGroup and aclose()
PRs missing backports.body:
Currently if you have a generator like:
```
async def test():
    async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
        async for x in whatever():
            yield x
```

If aclose() is called on the generator and GeneratorExit is raised,
the TaskGroup's `__aexit__` will raise a BaseExceptionGroup, and that
will be raised from the aclose() call instead of it being swallowed.

Fix this by raising GeneratorExit from __aexit__ when:
1. The body of task group raised it
2. No subtasks raised exceptions

This makes GeneratorExit work without swallowing other exceptions
(like it would if we just added it to _is_base_error).

PRs missing backports.title: gh-153291: Fix data race in readline.get_completer() and get_pre_input_hook()
PRs missing backports.body:
`readline.get_completer()` reads `state->completer` and returns a new reference without taking the module critical section, while `set_completer()` swaps the same field under the critical section with `Py_XSETREF`. On the free-threaded build a concurrent getter can be incrementing the refcount of a hook the setter is simultaneously dropping. `get_pre_input_hook()` has the same problem with `state->pre_input_hook` — those are the only two hook fields with both a `Py_XSETREF`-based setter and a Python-level getter, so this covers the whole Python-visible getter surface.

The fix adds `@critical_section` to both getters, the same way gh-126895 did for the rest of the module.

Verified with a free-threaded TSAN build (`--disable-gil --with-thread-sanitizer`): the reproducer from the issue reports the race on main (the `readline_get_completer` read vs the `set_hook` write) and runs clean with this change. The new tests in test_readline.py trigger the same TSAN reports without the fix and pass with it.

Deliberately not included here: `get_begidx()`/`get_endidx()` and the C callback paths (`on_completion()` etc.) read module state without the critical section too, but their writer/reader sides live in readline callbacks (`flex_complete()`, `on_hook()`), where taking the module critical section is a design question (it would serialize completion callbacks against all other readline calls) — that's a follow-up, not a one-line annotation.

I used AI assistance while working on this change; I've reviewed it and can explain it.

* Issue: gh-153291

PRs missing backports.body:
... even if there is an interrupt during the call to `mngr.__enter__()`

When checking the eval breaker after a call, don't break if the previous code unit has `opcode == LOAD_SPECIAL`.
Sometimes a cache will appear to be a `LOAD_SPECIAL`, but this is fine as this only applies to calls, and any loop will still have an eval breaker check on the back edge.
